answer: In an agent market trading goods such as sable and marble, each active seller identity must lock a $1,000 bond for 30 days before it can accept orders. An attacker can forge unlimited profiles, but cannot reuse the same locked funds across them: 1,000 live sybils require $1 million in escrow. The bond makes identity flooding capital-intensive, imposing financing costs even if every deposit is eventually refunded.
